text: This is Mobilis: collateral mobility on Canton. Four institutions share one ledger, and each sees only its own slice.
Step one. The pledgor posts a Treasury bill, one million face value. The ledger, not the browser, decides what it's worth.
The secured party agrees. Before it can, the ledger checks the move against the agreement's rules.
The custodian settles it atomically. After the two percent haircut, the ledger values it at nine hundred and eighty thousand.
Step two. The exposure moves, and the secured party calls for one point four million of collateral.
The custodian applies it. Coverage drops to seventy percent: the book is four hundred and twenty thousand short.
Can the custodian simply mark it fulfilled? No. The ledger checks that the book is actually covered, and refuses.
Step three. The pledgor tops up with a corporate bond. After a five percent haircut, coverage is back above one hundred percent.
Now the margin call can be marked fulfilled. The ledger confirms the book is covered.
Step four. The pledgor needs its Treasuries back for a repo. The collateral optimiser looks for the cheapest swap that the rules allow.
It rules out the tempting swaps and says why: corporate bonds would break their concentration limit, and high yield isn't eligible. Cash is the valid move.
One asset out, one in, in a single transaction. The secured party is never unprotected.
Step five. What if someone tries a bad swap? Here, the corporate bond is swapped for just one hundred dollars of cash.
The ledger refuses it. It can't even be agreed, because the rules live on the ledger itself.
Step six. Markets move. The custodian marks the corporate bond down to eighty, and the ledger re-values the whole book at once. It is now short.
Until it's topped up, every release is refused. The pledgor's screen proposes the cheapest top-up. One click, agreed, and settled.
Step seven. The custodian publishes the regulator's report, computed by the ledger at the latest price marks.
And the regulator sees that report, and nothing else: coverage, positions, breaches, and the valuation date. Its node never received the agreement or the calls.
Mobilis. Every collateral rule, enforced by the ledger. Built on Canton, for HackCanton season three.
